_why: The directive is model-authored text, which is untrusted input, and its parsed attribute becomes the argument to klausSwitchSession. So every rejection case is pinned here: anything that is not exactly one well-formed directive on its own line stays visible text. That is the deliberate asymmetry — showing the user raw protocol syntax is a cosmetic wart, while swallowing a sentence the model wrote deletes content they were owed, and raising a card for a directive the model was merely DISCUSSING (inside a code fence) navigates somewhere the user never asked to go. Klaus accepts only threadId: create_thread builds the worktree BEFORE starting the conversation and always returns a real thread id, so a clientThreadId form would render a card nothing could resolve.

accepts.name: trailing whitespace on the line is tolerated
a non-uuid id still parses: the host decides existence, not the syntax
an id containing angle brackets and ampersand parses unescaped

rejects.name: ordinary prose
rejects.line: I created a chat for you.

rejects.name: the prefix alone with no attributes
a single colon instead of two
a second unknown attribute alongside threadId
a clientThreadId form, which Klaus never emits
an over-long id past the 512 bound

markdownStructure.name: a standalone directive becomes its own paragraph, which is what the card pass looks for
a directive inside a fenced block stays code and never becomes a paragraph
a directive inside a tilde fence stays code
an inline code span keeps the directive as text
a directive sharing a paragraph with prose is not its own paragraph
